maria-cs: heads-up — Acme reported a 422 on our /v1/rerank endpoint. They say all returned scores are 0 and the payload error mentions an ambiguous 'query' field. ticket #C-4321 :grimacing:

maria-cs: pasted their payload below, redacted ids:
```json
{
  "query": "how to reset password",
  "documents": [
    {
      "id": "doc-1",
      "title": "Reset flow",
      "passages": [ { "text": "step 1..." } ],
      "query": "internal_context"
    }
  ],
  "candidates": [
    { "text": "Use settings > account > reset", "metadata": { "source": "kb" } }
  ]
}
```

kevin-eng: thanks — yep looks like they put a nested "query" inside a document. our parser flattens/merges query keys and ends up treating the top-level query as ambiguous. that can cause the validation to throw or produce zeroed scores. quick fix is to rename nested keys or move that field under metadata.

jess-ml: can reproduce locally — created a minimal repro by sending that exact shape to the rerank service and got a 422 with message: "ambiguous query field (top-level vs nested)". after removing document.query the results return expected scores.

samir-sre: what about backwards compatibility? some customers store contextual fields called "query" inside docs. we shouldn't break them silently.

kevin-eng: agreed. short-term: advise customer to rename nested field (e.g., document.context_query) as workaround. mid-term: ML/runtime should validate and prefer top-level query and ignore nested keys with a warning in the response, or return a clearer error pointing to offending path.

maria-cs: I told Acme the rename workaround and asked for permission to run a repro payload. they said ok — gave us a dev token.

support-bot: ticket C-4321 updated: assigned to kevin-eng. link: https://redwood.support/tickets/C-4321

kevin-eng: quick notes for the patch I plan to try:
- update validation to detect duplicate key names across object paths (e.g., /query vs /documents/*/query) and return a 422 with an explicit error_path field in the body.
- emit an info log with the customer id + offending path so support can suggest minimal payload edits.

jess-ml: repro steps I ran:
1) run: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer $DEV_TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @payload.json
2) payload.json = the JSON above (with nested document.query)
3) saw 422: {"error":"ambiguous query field", "message":"conflicting 'query' keys: top-level and documents[0].query" }

kevin-eng: I'll throw up a tiny validator patch and a unit test. if it looks good we'll ship to staging and then roll to prod behind a flag.

maria-cs: customer wants to know ETA — can you give a rough timeline?

kevin-eng: aiming for a short PR today, staging tomorrow, prod rollout early next week behind flag. I'll post updates here. :thumbsup:

samir-sre: also double-check the batch limit behaviour — if a payload contains both passages and candidates we should ensure batching chooses the correct scoring route; weird shapes have triggered degenerate scores in the past.

jess-ml: noted, I'll add an e2e that mixes candidates/documents/passages permutations and assert non-zero scores for valid inputs.

maria-cs: perfect. I'll keep Acme posted and mark ticket as "investigating". thanks team.

kevin-eng: update 1718043720 — pushed validator branch to staging, tests pass, creating canary job. will post canary link when ready.

support-bot: ticket C-4321 status changed: investigating -> patching.
